# HAProxy — root-context-push-url-sse

root-context-sse with VAADIN_PUSH_URL=/VAADIN/push. Identical to root-context-sse: over SSE there is no upgrade to arrange, and the frontend carries the event stream and the client-to-server POSTs alike.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

HAProxy config (`haproxy/templates/passthrough-sse.cfg`), mounted as
`conf.d/10-vaadin.cfg`:

```haproxy
# passthrough.cfg plus a refusal to upgrade, for the *-sse scenarios:
#
#   root-context-sse            app at /,    proxy at /
#   root-context-push-url-sse   the same, with VAADIN_PUSH_URL=/VAADIN/push
#   custom-context-sse          app on /app, proxy preserves the path
#
# The Apache and NGINX *-sse configs refuse by omission: Upgrade and Connection
# are hop-by-hop headers that neither proxy forwards unless a directive puts
# them back, and those configs simply do not. HAProxy relays an upgrade with no
# configuration at all and has no keyword to stop it, so the refusal has to be
# written out — which also means the 501 comes from the proxy rather than from
# Atmosphere. Traefik has the same problem and solves it the third way, by
# deleting the client's Upgrade header with a middleware.
#
# SSE still works, because it is an ordinary HTTP GET that streams
# text/event-stream, and the client-to-server messages are XHR POSTs to the
# same path. Selecting a WebSocket transport here fails, which is the point of
# the scenario rather than a bug.
frontend vaadin-in from vaadin-front
    bind :80
    http-request deny deny_status 501 if { req.hdr(Upgrade) -m found }
    default_backend vaadin-app

backend vaadin-app from vaadin
    server vaadin vaadin:8080
```

The `global` section, and the two `defaults` sections this file
inherits from, come from the shared
[haproxy-base.cfg](../../haproxy-base.cfg), mounted read-only beside
it as `conf.d/00-base.cfg`. Base and scenario only parse as a pair.
